newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila o/night rate down slightly as demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Manila o/night rate down slightly as demand eases.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call rate dipped slightly to 11.0625 percent from yesterday's 11.09375 percent as demand for overnight money eased, traders said.
"It's a slow day. The market is very liquid," one trader said. The rate has been hovering slightly above the Central Bank's rate of 11.0 percent.
Turnover remained thin at 12.913 billion pesos with done rates ranging between 11.03125 percent and 11.1875 percent.
Twenty three institutions were on the lending side, while 21 financial institutions tapped the interbank market for funds.
The secondary market for government securities was active with several banks buying longer-termed Treasury bills.

Bid rates for one-year bills ranged from 12.55 to 12.7 percent, while offered rates were bounded between 12.55 to 12.675 percent. The rates were lower than this week's average auction rate of 12.688 percent.
"Many banks believe that the rate has reached its peak this week, especially after the Bureau of Treasury announced that it's going to cut down the offering size," she said.
The Treasury is cutting down the offering size to only 1.5 billion pesos from 2.5 billion pesos.
Bid rates for six-month bills ranged from 11.95 to 12.25 percent, while offered rates were at 11.9 to 12.10 percent.
Three-month bills were being bid with effective rates ranging from 11.45 to 11.65 percent, while offered rates were 11.525 to 11.65 percent.
